entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen29324" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen29325" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen29326" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen29326" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen29325" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen29327" type="x-p"/> The prophet, having described the judgments impending over his countrymen, enlarges on the corruptions which prevailed among them. Their profession of religion was all false and hypocritical, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.1">Jer 5:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.2">Jer 5:2</reference>. Though corrected, they were not amended, but persisted in their guilt, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.3">Jer 5:3</reference>. This was not the case with the low and ignorant only, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.4">Jer 5:4</reference>; but more egregiously so with those of the higher order, from whose knowledge and opportunities better things might have been expected, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.5">Jer 5:5</reference>. God therefore threatens them with the most cruel enemies, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.6">Jer 5:6</reference>; and appeals to themselves if they should be permitted to practice such sins unpunished, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.7-Jer.5.9">Jer 5:7-9</reference>. He then commands their enemies to raze the walls of Jerusalem, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.10">Jer 5:10</reference>; that devoted city whose inhabitants added to all their other sins the highest contempt of God's word and prophets, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.11-Jer.5.13">Jer 5:11-13</reference>. Wherefore his word, in the mouth of his prophet, shall be as fire to consume them, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.14">Jer 5:14</reference>; the Chaldean forces shall cruelly addict them, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.15-Jer.5.17">Jer 5:15-17</reference>; and farther judgments await then as the consequence of their apostasy and idolatry, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.18">Jer 5:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.19">Jer 5:19</reference>. The chapter closes with a most melancholy picture of the moral condition of the Jewish people at that period which immediately preceded the Babylonish captivity, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.20-Jer.5.31">Jer 5:20-31</reference>. <div eID="gen29327" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29328" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen29328" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29329" type="x-p"/> Broad places - Market-places, and those where there was most public resort. <div eID="gen29329" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29330" type="x-p"/> If ye can find a man - A certain philosopher went through the streets of Athens with a lighted lamp in his hand; and being asked what he sought, answered, "I am seeking to find a Man." So in Jerusalem none was found, on the most diligent search, who acted worthy the character of a rational being. <div eID="gen29330" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29331" type="x-p"/> I will pardon it - I will spare the city for the sake of one righteous person. So at the intercession of Abraham, God would have spared Sodom if there had been ten righteous persons found in it; <reference osisRef="Gen.18.26">Gen 18:26</reference>.
entries.content_plain: Introduction The prophet, having described the judgments impending over his countrymen, enlarges on the corruptions which prevailed among them. Their profession of religion was all false and hypocritical, Jer 5:1 , Jer 5:2 . Though corrected, they were not amended, but persisted in their guilt, Jer 5:3 . This was not the case with the low and ignorant only, Jer 5:4 ; but more egregiously so with those of the higher order, from whose knowledge and opportunities better things might have been expected, Jer 5:5 . God therefore threatens them with the most cruel enemies, Jer 5:6 ; and appeals to themselves if they should be permitted to practice such sins unpunished, Jer 5:7-9 . He then commands their enemies to raze the walls of Jerusalem, Jer 5:10 ; that devoted city whose inhabitants added to all their other sins the highest contempt of God's word and prophets, Jer 5:11-13 . Wherefore his word, in the mouth of his prophet, shall be as fire to consume them, Jer 5:14 ; the Chaldean forces shall cruelly addict them, Jer 5:15-17 ; and farther judgments await then as the consequence of their apostasy and idolatry, Jer 5:18 , Jer 5:19 . The chapter closes with a most melancholy picture of the moral condition of the Jewish people at that period which immediately preceded the Babylonish captivity, Jer 5:20-31 . Verse 1 Broad places - Market-places, and those where there was most public resort. If ye can find a man - A certain philosopher went through the streets of Athens with a lighted lamp in his hand; and being asked what he sought, answered, "I am seeking to find a Man." So in Jerusalem none was found, on the most diligent search, who acted worthy the character of a rational being. I will pardon it - I will spare the city for the sake of one righteous person. So at the intercession of Abraham, God would have spared Sodom if there had been ten righteous persons found in it; Gen 18:26 .

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen29331" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29332" type="x-p"/> The Lord liveth - Though they profess to bind themselves by Jehovah, as if they acknowledged him their God and only Lord, yet they swore falsely; for not believing in him, they took a false oath; one by which they did not believe themselves bound, not acknowledging him as their Lord. entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen29333" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29334" type="x-p"/> I will get me unto the great men - Those whose circumstances and rank in life gave them opportunities of information which the others could not have, for the reasons already given. <div eID="gen29334" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29335" type="x-p"/> These have altogether broken the yoke - These have cast aside all restraint, have acted above law, and have trampled all moral obligations under their feet, and into their vortex the lower classes of the people have been swept away. Solon said, "The laws are like cobwebs; they entangle the small fry, but the great ones go through them, and carry all away with them."

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen29338" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29339" type="x-p"/> Go ye up upon her walls - This is the permission and authority given to the Chaldeans to pillage Jerusalem. <div eID="gen29339" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29340" type="x-p"/> Take away her battlements - Some translate נטישות netishoth, branches; others, vines. Destroy the branches, cut down the stem; but do not damage the root. Leave so many of the people that the state may be regenerated. The Septuagint, Syriac, and Arabic, read, "Leave her foundations, for they are the Lord's;" and this agrees with "Destroy, but make not a full end."

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen29340" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29341" type="x-p"/> They have belied the Lord - כחשו kichashu. They have denied or disavowed the Lord. <div eID="gen29341" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29342" type="x-p"/> It is not he - לוא הוא lo hu, he is not; there is no such being; therefore this evil shall not come upon us. On their premises, this conclusion was just. There is no judge; therefore there shall be no judgment. Thus they denied the Lord. They were atheists at heart.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen29342" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29343" type="x-p"/> And the prophets shall become wind - What are the prophets? <div eID="gen29343" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29344" type="x-p"/> Empty persons. Their words are wind; we hear the sound of their threatening but of the matter of the threatenings we shall hear no more. <div eID="gen29344" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29345" type="x-p"/> And the word is not in them - There is no inspirer, but may their own predictions fall on their own heads! This seems the natural sense of this passage.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen29350" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29351" type="x-p"/> Which have placed the sand for the bound of the sea - What can I not do, who confine the sea, that enormous mass of waters, and prevent it from overflowing the earth; not by immense mountains and rocks, but by the sand, no particle of which is in cohesion with another? The most tremendous waves cannot displace nor pass over this simple barrier.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 24</hi> <div eID="gen29352" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29353" type="x-p"/> Giveth rain, both the former and the latter - See the note on <reference osisRef="Jer.3.3">Jer 3:3</reference>. <div eID="gen29353" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29354" type="x-p"/> The appointed weeks of the harvest - As the early rains fell in the northern parts of Judea about the end of September, in the civil year of the Hebrews, so the latter rains fell before harvest, in the months of March and April. The appointed weeks of the harvest were those which fell between the passover and pentecost. In the southern parts the harvest was earlier than in the northern. Dr. Blayney translates, "A sufficiency of the appointed things of harvest he secureth to us." <div eID="gen29354" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29355" type="x-p"/> If the word שבעת weeks, be read with a ש sin instead of a ש shin, it will signify fullness or sufficiency; and thus the Septuagint and Vulgate have read it. I think the present reading is much to be preferred. God appoints a harvest time, and in his good providence he generally gives harvest weather.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 31</hi> <div eID="gen29360" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29361" type="x-p"/> The prophets prophesy falsely - The false prophets predict favorable things, that they may please both the princes and the people. <div eID="gen29361" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29362" type="x-p"/> The priests bear rule by their means - The false prophets affording them all that their influence and power can procure, to enable them to keep their places, and feed on the riches of the Lord's house. <div eID="gen29362" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29363" type="x-p"/> And my people love to have it so - Are perfectly satisfied with this state of things, because they are permitted to continue in their sins without reproof or restraint. The prophets and the priests united to deceive and ruin the people. The prophets gave out false predictions; by their means the priests got the government of the people into their own hands; and so infatuated were the people that they willingly abandoned themselves to those blind guides, and would not hearken to the voice of any reformer. In my Old Bible the words stand thus: - Stonyng and mervailis ben made in the erthe, prophets prophecieden lesing; and prestis flappiden with joye with ther bondes, and my peple lovid siche thingis. False prophets and worldly priests have been in all ages the bane of religion, and the ruin of many souls. When profligate people stand up on behalf of profligate priests, corruption must then be at its height.  <chapter eID="Jer.5"/> <div eID="gen29363" type="x-p"/>

navigation_sections.title: Introduction
navigation_sections.content_plain: Introduction The prophet, having described the judgments impending over his countrymen, enlarges on the corruptions which prevailed among them. Their profession of religion was all false and hypocritical, Jer 5:1 , Jer 5:2 . Though corrected, they were not amended, but persisted in their guilt, Jer 5:3 . This was not the case with the low and ignorant only, Jer 5:4 ; but more egregiously so with those of the higher order, from whose knowledge and opportunities better things might have been expected, Jer 5:5 . God therefore threatens them with the most cruel enemies, Jer 5:6 ; and appeals to themselves if they should be permitted to practice such sins unpunished, Jer 5:7-9 . He then commands their enemies to raze the walls of Jerusalem, Jer 5:10 ; that devoted city whose inhabitants added to all their other sins the highest contempt of God's word and prophets, Jer 5:11-13 . Wherefore his word, in the mouth of his prophet, shall be as fire to consume them, Jer 5:14 ; the Chaldean forces shall cruelly addict them, Jer 5:15-17 ; and farther judgments await then as the consequence of their apostasy and idolatry, Jer 5:18 , Jer 5:19 . The chapter closes with a most melancholy picture of the moral condition of the Jewish people at that period which immediately preceded the Babylonish captivity, Jer 5:20-31 .
